title: Alpha's First Reviews Are In — and Hrithik Roshan Just Stole a Film He's Barely In
excerpt: The CBFC premiere has critics calling it 'gripping' and 'visually spectacular.' But everyone's talking about those twelve seconds of green eyes.
body:
Here's what we know about **Alpha** before it hits theatres tomorrow: **Alia Bhatt** looks like she could actually kill you. **Sharvari** matches her blow for blow. **Bobby Deol** chews scenery like it's his last meal. And somewhere in the film's 140 minutes, **Hrithik Roshan** walks in as Kabir — the same Kabir from *War* — and the room apparently erupted.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=QRqGwGwo1Y0</youtube>

The film premiered at the CBFC screening earlier this week, and the early word is… surprisingly good. Film critic Kuldeep Gadhvi rated it 4 out of 5, calling it "a refreshing female-led action entertainer that never feels like a gimmick." That last part matters. After the franchise stumbled badly with *War 2* and *Tiger 3* fell flat, plenty of people had written the **YRF Spy Universe** off entirely. *Alpha* was supposed to release Christmas 2025. Then it got pushed to April 2026. Then July. Every delay felt like another nail in the coffin.

And yet.

> "Alia once again proves why she is one of the finest performers of her generation. She brings conviction, intensity, vulnerability, and charisma to the role of Alpha, carrying the film with complete confidence." — Kuldeep Gadhvi

That's high praise for an actress who needed exactly this. *Jigra* disappointed. The whispers about her box office appeal grew louder. *Alpha* gives her something she hasn't had in a while: a physical, commanding, no-nonsense role where charisma alone won't cut it — she has to fight. And from what early viewers are saying, she does.

But let's talk about the moment everyone is actually buzzing about.

**Hrithik Roshan's cameo as Kabir** — the super-agent from the *War* films — was always teased in the trailer, which closed on a shot of a mysterious figure in white with unmistakable green eyes. The CBFC screening confirmed it: he's in the film, his entry is brief, and critics are calling it "whistle-worthy." In an industry where cameos often feel like contractual obligations, this one apparently lands like a grenade. You see him, the audience screams, and he vanishes. Perfect.

**Sharvari**, meanwhile, is carrying her own weight. Coming off a strong showing in *Munjya* and *Main Vaapas Aaunga*, she's on the kind of streak that builds real stardom — the quiet, earned kind. In *Alpha*, she's paired with Bollywood's most celebrated actress, and by all early accounts, she doesn't blink. One unverified review did suggest Alia "overshadows" her, sparking a brief social media flare-up that Sharvari herself had defused months earlier:

> "She is an incredible human being first and foremost, and a brilliant actor. To be able to just work with her and headline a film like Alpha means the world to me." — Sharvari

The fan theories, predictably, are going wild. Since the trailer, viewers have speculated that Sharvari's character might be **Ruhi** — the daughter of Vaani Kapoor's character from the *War* franchise, whose guardian is Kabir (Hrithik). If true, it would thread *Alpha* into the Spy Universe's mythology more deeply than any entry since *Pathaan*. The filmmakers are saying nothing, which in Bollywood usually means it's true.

The CBFC gave the film a UA 16+ certificate after censoring multiple stabbing visuals and deleting a profanity. It runs 140 minutes — lean for a franchise film — shot across Mumbai, Kashmir's Sonamarg and Pahalgam, Scotland, and Poland. **Anil Kapoor** plays a mentor figure linked to the Alpha programme, while **Bobby Deol's** villain Fateh runs a shadowy operation that turns against India.

Advance bookings are tracking around ₹7 crore for opening day — modest by Spy Universe standards, where *Pathaan* opened at ₹55 crore and *War* at ₹51 crore. But this is a female-led action film releasing in a market that hasn't always been kind to that proposition. The real test isn't Day 1. It's the weekend trajectory. If word-of-mouth holds — and these first reactions suggest it will — ₹7 crore could easily become ₹30-plus for the opening weekend.

For diaspora audiences in the US, UK, and Canada, *Alpha* opens wide tomorrow, July 3 — landing right on the Fourth of July corridor in America, which historically treats Bollywood releases well. It's screening in Hindi across multiplex chains and select premium-format screens.

The Spy Universe bet everything on two women this time. Based on what the first audiences are saying, it might have been the smartest bet YRF has made in years.
